source: test fixture — issue #260: a rival substance whose name occurs in an answer only as a SUBSTRING of a longer word
description: Two substances, one of which publishes a daily ceiling. Paracetamol carries a 4000 mg/day ceiling, so a stated 1500 mg four times daily is 6000 and must warn; Penicillin publishes no band and is here only to be the rival whose alias the answer's wording does or does not carry. The pair is chosen because 'penicillin' occurs inside the plural 'penicillins' — a form a clinical answer routinely uses and which the module's own prose rule (DrugReference.containsWord, zero trailing letters) does not treat as naming the drug, while String.indexOf does. Different level-4 ATC subgroups so the class arm raises nothing beside the dose warning. What no bundled dataset can pose is the RIVAL, not the ceiling: the shipped curated seed publishes the same 4000 mg/day adult ceiling for Paracetamol, but none of its twelve aliases is one a clinical answer would write in a form that nests it the way 'penicillins' nests 'penicillin'. substanceName is set on both entries only so the cases run the substance-keyed grouping a ddinter deployment would; it is not required, since substanceGroupKey falls back to the row itself.
